sections.section_name: Section A - Choose the Correct Answer

questions.question_text: Which of these is a texture you might find in nature?
When drawing an underwater 'Aqua World' scene, which colour would be the most common?
If you want to show 'People in Action' running fast, what should you draw?
options: A) A person sitting still on a chair
B) A person sleeping in bed
C) A person with bent knees and swinging arms
D) A person standing perfectly straight
questions.answer: C) A person with bent knees and swinging arms

questions.question_text: What do we call the way objects are grouped and placed together in art?
Which tool is best for blending dry pastel colours smoothly on paper?
What feeling does a smooth, curvy, wavy line often give in a drawing?
When you 'Look Around' to draw a landscape outside, what is usually at the very top of your paper?
Which of these materials is best for making a 3D nature collage?
options: B) Watercolours and a thin brush
C) Leaves, twigs, and craft glue
D) A computer mouse and keyboard
questions.answer: C) Leaves, twigs, and craft glue

questions.question_text: If you imagine a magical, unreal forest, which colour might you paint the leaves to show it is fantasy?
In a drawing of a small apple sitting next to a tall water jug, which one should usually be drawn taller on the page?
options: B) Both should be exactly the same height

questions.question_text: Describe the texture of a real leaf compared to a plastic water bottle. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A real leaf feels slightly bumpy, veiny, and natural when you touch it. A plastic bottle feels very smooth, hard, and slippery under your fingers.

questions.question_text: What are two things you would include in a drawing of an 'Aqua World'? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: I would include colourful, striped fish swimming near the sandy bottom. I would also draw long green seaweed waving gently in the bright blue water.

questions.question_text: How do you draw a person who is jumping up in the air? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: To draw a jumping person, I make their feet point downwards, away from the ground line. Their arms are drawn thrown up high in the air.

questions.question_text: Why is it important to look at the arrangement of objects before painting a still life? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: It helps you see how things overlap and fit together perfectly. You can check if the shapes look balanced and interesting on your drawing paper.

questions.question_text: Name a performing art (like music or dance) and one way you can show it in a painting. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Dance is a performing art. I can paint a dancer with a flowing red dress and lifted arms to show the fast, beautiful movement of the dance.

questions.question_text: Imagine you have discovered a new planet. Describe the landscape and the shapes of the plants there. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The new planet has a bright orange sky with three tiny moons. The ground is covered in shiny silver sand. The plants are shaped like giant spirals and triangles instead of normal trees, and they have glowing pink dots that light up in the dark.

questions.question_text: Think of a crowded marketplace. Describe what you see when you 'Look Around' and how people are positioned. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Looking around, I see tall market stalls covered in large yellow umbrellas. Some people are standing straight, carrying heavy bags of vegetables. Others are sitting on small wooden stools, leaning forward to talk loudly. A few children are running quickly through the narrow dirt paths.

questions.question_text: Describe step-by-step how you would create a mixed-media artwork using textures found in nature. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: First, I would walk in a park and carefully collect dry brown leaves, pieces of rough tree bark, and tiny smooth pebbles. Then, I would take a large piece of thick chart paper and spread liquid glue over it. I would press the leaves flat, stick the bark to make a tree trunk, and arrange the pebbles to create a textured path.

questions.question_text: How would you use different lines and colours to show the feeling of a loud, angry storm in a drawing? [50-60 words]
questions.answer: I would use dark colours like black, deep purple, and dark grey to make the clouds look heavy and scary. Instead of smooth lines, I would draw sharp, jagged zig-zag lines in bright yellow to show the lightning strikes. I would use thick, heavy pencil strokes slanting downwards very quickly to look like harsh, fast rain hitting the ground.
